story.tutorial.name: Basic training
story.tutorial.desc: Six short parts: moving, staying alive, mining, crafting, research and flying.
story.tutorial.graduated: Basic training complete! You can survive, build, research and fly — short courses wait in your Journal.
story.tutorial.refresher: Your training log looks thin. Want a quick refresher? Open the Journal and restart the tutorial there.
story.tutorial.ask_skip: Want me to show you the basics? If you know the game already, you can skip the training.
story.tutorial.skipped_hint: All right, no training. If you ever want it, it waits in your Journal.
story.tutorial.cut.launch.title: Lift-off!
story.tutorial.cut.launch.space: Space begins right above the clouds
story.tutorial.cut.landing.sub: Every world has its own rocks, plants and creatures.
story.tutorial.cut.dock.inside: Vendors and a mission board wait inside
story.tutorial.cut.jump.unknown: Unknown stars show “?” until you have been there
story.tutorial.cut.base.title: Your home
story.tutorial.cut.base.sub: Walls keep animals away — and on airless worlds, sealed rooms hold air.
story.tutorial.cut.ship.title: Your own ship
story.tutorial.cut.ship.sub: Built by you, block by block — and it flies.
story.tutorial.cut.circuit.title: It works!
story.tutorial.cut.tame.title: A new friend!
story.tutorial.ch.b1.sum: Walking, looking around, VEGA, the quick bar, the menu and the Codex.
story.tutorial.ch.b2.sum: Health, air and food, the way back to your ship, the lamp — and what happens if you faint.
story.tutorial.ch.b3.sum: Mining, iron ore, rock that is too hard, your backpack, your gear and the cargo hold.
story.tutorial.ch.b4.sum: The ship's workshop, iron ingots and plates, placing and turning blocks, a campfire.
story.tutorial.ch.b5.sum: Scanning, knowledge, your first blueprint and data fragments.
story.tutorial.ch.b6.sum: Launching, flying, the ship scanner, docking, trading, a first job, landing and flying home.
story.tutorial.ch.c2.sum: New discoveries, data caches, what blueprints cost, DataQube games, rune stones, the terrain scanner and your achievements.
story.tutorial.ch.c3.sum: Waypoints, scanning a world before you land, breaking asteroids, walking inside your ship and going on a spacewalk.
story.tutorial.ch.c4.sum: Docking at a station, vendors and their trades, the mission board, undocking and handing in a job.
story.tutorial.ch.c5.sum: Markers and map travel, a forge and lubricant, the jump generator, your first hyperjump, wormholes and wrecks.
story.tutorial.ch.c1.sum: Rock that is too hard, titanium ore from your ship's trade console, a forge and your first titanium plate.
story.tutorial.ch.c6.sum: Ship modules, repairing the hull, growing your ship — then one of your own: the Shipwright blueprint, a keel, commissioning and your fleet.
story.tutorial.ch.c7.sum: Your own base: a base core, building in its zone, lights, a door, air in a sealed room, a wall ring and a bed to wake up in.
story.tutorial.ch.c17.sum: A station core deployed on a spacewalk, a hull and an airlock around it, and floating while you build.
story.tutorial.ch.c8.sum: The Crystal Net and VEGA's six workshop jobs: a lamp, a doorbell, a night light, an airlock, a little factory and a secret door — each with its reward.
story.tutorial.ch.c14.sum: Crafting in bulk at a factory's terminal, claiming a factory with an SPS code, and a fabricator that works by itself — even while you are away.
story.tutorial.ch.c9.sum: Scanning animals, feeding a begging herd, taming a companion and looking after it.
story.tutorial.ch.c10.sum: Planting seeds and saplings, a campfire, samples from everything you harvest, and the bio lab.
story.tutorial.ch.c11.sum: Talking to settlers, answers that make friends, the people you know and who helps with what.
story.tutorial.ch.c12.sum: Fending off what attacks you and chasing robbers away — only where this world has them, and always your choice.
story.tutorial.ch.c13.sum: Climbing walls, the rope gun, jetpack and glider, a boat or a speeder, trains, beam pads and lifts.
story.tutorial.ch.c15.sum: Chat and radios, trading with players, allies and crews, pings — and what to do if someone is unkind.
story.tutorial.ch.c16.sum: Painting blocks, new forms and colours, copying whole builds — and your own look.
story.tutorial.ch.c18.sum: How to find things: chests and caches, ruins and wrecks, settlers' tips, data cubes and wrecks in space.
story.tutorial.b1.walk.start: Let's start with walking: take a few steps ({key:Move}) and look around ({key:Look}).
story.tutorial.b1.walk.hint: Walk with {key:Move} in any direction — a few steps are enough.
story.tutorial.b1.jump.start: Jump with {key:Jump}. Crouch with {key:Crouch} — then you won't slip off edges.
story.tutorial.b1.jump.start_fly: Jump with {key:Jump} — press it twice quickly to fly. Crouch with {key:Crouch} to stop at edges.
story.tutorial.b1.vega.start: I'm VEGA, your ship's AI. The bar at the top always shows your current goal. Press {key:VegaContinue} to go on.
story.tutorial.b1.vega.start_story: I'm VEGA, your ship's AI — what's left of me. The bar at the top shows your goal. Press {key:VegaContinue} to go on.
story.tutorial.b1.hotbar.start: Your quick bar: slot 1 holds the drill, slot 2 the scanner. Pick slot 2 ({key:Hotbar}), then slot 1 again.
story.tutorial.b1.menu.start: Everything you carry and build lives in your menu. Open it with {key:UiMenu}.
story.tutorial.b1.codex.start: Stuck? The Codex explains everything — it's at the top of the menu. Open it once.
story.tutorial.b1.codex.start_story: Stuck? The Codex at the top of the menu explains everything. I wrote it before the crash. Open it once.
story.tutorial.b2.bars.start: Watch your three bars: health, air and food. Air refills aboard and in fresh air.
story.tutorial.b2.bars.start_health: Keep an eye on your health bar — air and food never run out here.
story.tutorial.b2.bars.start_no_air: Watch your bars for health and food — air never runs out here.
story.tutorial.b2.bars.start_no_food: Watch your bars for health and air. Air refills aboard and in fresh air.
story.tutorial.b2.eat.start: Hungry? Select food in your quick bar — you start with berries — and eat it ({key:Place}).
story.tutorial.b2.eat.hint: Food is in your quick bar or your backpack. Select it, then {key:Place} eats it.
story.tutorial.b2.berries.start: Green plants and bushes drop berries. Gather 3 more — just mine the plants ({key:Mine}).
story.tutorial.b2.berries.hint: Look for green bushes or flowers close by. Breaking them gives berries.
story.tutorial.b2.ration.start: Your suit just fed you a ration. It carries two and feeds you when you're very hungry. Any food refills it.
story.tutorial.b2.home.start: The blue square on your compass is your ship. Walk away a bit, then find your way back to it.
story.tutorial.b2.home.chip: Walk away, then back to the ship
story.tutorial.b2.home.hint: Lost? The pause menu has “Back to my ship”. Or turn until the blue square is on top, then walk.
story.tutorial.b2.home.hint_teleporter: Lost? Your teleporter takes you straight back to the ship.
story.tutorial.b2.home.hint_compass: Lost? Turn until the blue square sits on top of your compass, then walk towards it.
story.tutorial.b2.lamp.start: Dark cave or night? Switch your suit lamp on and off with {key:ToggleLamp}.
story.tutorial.b2.climate.start: Your suit is fighting the cold or the heat right now. A roof, a cave or your ship helps it.
story.tutorial.b2.faint.start: You fainted and woke up again, safe and sound. It happens — just carry on.
story.tutorial.b3.mine.start: Pick the drill (slot 1), aim at a block and hold {key:Mine}. Mine 3 blocks.
story.tutorial.b3.iron.start: Iron ore sits a few blocks underground — look for rusty spots. Mine 4 iron ore.
story.tutorial.b3.iron.hint: No iron yet? Dig straight down a few blocks, or look along cave walls for rusty spots.
story.tutorial.b3.tier.start: Too hard for your drill! Better tools come from blueprints — scan the block to see which one you need.
story.tutorial.b3.backpack.start: In your menu ({key:UiMenu}), pick an item in your backpack, then pick a new slot for it.
story.tutorial.b3.backpack.chip: Move an item in your backpack
story.tutorial.b3.gear.start: Gear only works while you wear it. Menu, Inventory, Suit: take your lamp off, then put it back on.
story.tutorial.b3.gear.chip: Take your lamp off and on again
story.tutorial.b3.gear.hint: Your suit gear is under menu ({key:UiMenu}), Inventory, Suit. Pick the lamp to take it off.
story.tutorial.b3.hold.start: Backpack full! Stow things in your ship's cargo hold: walk up to it and press {key:Interact}.
story.tutorial.b4.ingot.start: At your ship's workshop open the menu ({key:UiMenu}), Crafting: make 2 iron ingots.
story.tutorial.b4.ingot.start_free: Crafting is free here. Open the menu ({key:UiMenu}), Crafting, and make 2 iron ingots.
story.tutorial.b4.ingot.hint: Stand next to the workshop in your ship. Each ingredient shows whether you can craft it or it is raw.
story.tutorial.b4.plate.start: Two ingots make one iron plate. Craft a plate the same way.
story.tutorial.b4.place.start: Building: pick a block in your quick bar and place it with {key:Place}. Place 3 blocks.
story.tutorial.b4.rotate.start: Shaped blocks like stairs turn with {key:RotateShape}. Place one turned another way.
story.tutorial.b4.rotate.start_later: Later you'll build with shaped blocks like stairs and slopes. {key:RotateShape} turns them before you place them.
story.tutorial.b4.campfire.start: A campfire needs no station: 4 wood logs and 2 stone. Craft one in the menu and place it.
story.tutorial.b4.campfire.hint: Wood comes from trees — break a trunk with {key:Mine}.
story.tutorial.b5.scan.start: Pick the scanner (slot 2), aim at a plant, rock or animal and press {key:Scan}.
story.tutorial.b5.knowledge.start: Things you scan for the first time give knowledge. Scan 3 new things — the readout says edible or toxic.
story.tutorial.b5.research.start: Knowledge opens blueprints; research costs materials. At your cockpit: menu ({key:UiMenu}), Blueprints.
story.tutorial.b5.research.hint: The cheapest is the Paint Tool: 4 berries and 1 iron plate. Research it at your own cockpit.
story.tutorial.b5.fragments.start: Bigger blueprints also need data fragments. You find them in data caches, wrecks and ruins.
story.tutorial.b6.launch.start: Time to fly! Go to your ship's cockpit, press {key:Interact} and choose Launch.
story.tutorial.b6.fly.start: Steer with {key:Move} and {key:Look}. The chart ({key:FlightMap}) sets waypoints. Fly a little way.
story.tutorial.b6.shipscan.start: Your ship has a scanner on the last slot of the flight bar. Hold fire on an asteroid until the ring is full.
story.tutorial.b6.dock.start: See the station on your radar? Fly close and press {key:Interact} near it — the ship parks itself.
story.tutorial.b6.vendor.start: No station around here — no problem. Trade with a vendor in a settlement instead.
story.tutorial.b6.vendor.hint: Settlements have vendors. Talk to one with {key:Interact}, then choose Trade.
story.tutorial.b6.trade.start: Traders swap goods. Talk to a vendor with {key:Interact}, choose Trade and make one swap.
story.tutorial.b6.job.start: The mission board has jobs. Take one — the menu's Missions tab keeps track of it.
story.tutorial.b6.job.chip: Take a job from a board
story.tutorial.b6.land.start: Fly close to another world and press {key:Interact}: its landing map opens. Pick a pad and land.
story.tutorial.b6.pad.start: Time to practise landing: fly to a world, press {key:Interact} near it and pick a landing pad.
story.tutorial.b6.home.start: Worlds you've visited are on the map. Open it in the menu and travel home — the ship flies itself.
story.tutorial.b6.home.start_instant: The map takes you to any world in one go. Open it in the menu and travel home.
story.tutorial.c1.wall.start: Titanium ore is too hard for your drill — and the Titanium Drill needs titanium plates itself. The way round: your ship's trade console and a forge.
story.tutorial.c1.wall.start_free: Crafting is free here, but this is still the way to titanium: your ship's trade console swaps iron ore for titanium ore, a forge makes plates of it.
story.tutorial.c1.ore.start: Aboard, your ship's trade console swaps 5 iron ore for 1 titanium ore. Make that swap twice: menu ({key:UiMenu}), Crafting.
story.tutorial.c1.ore.chip: Swap iron ore for 2 titanium ore
story.tutorial.c1.ore.hint: Short of iron ore? It sits a few blocks down in the rock. 10 iron ore buy 2 titanium ore — enough for one plate.
story.tutorial.c1.forge.start: Titanium ore needs a forge to become plates. Craft one at your ship's workshop: 6 stone and 4 iron plates — no blueprint needed.
story.tutorial.c1.plate.start: Place your forge on a world ({key:Place}), stand next to it and smelt 2 titanium ore into a titanium plate: menu ({key:UiMenu}), Crafting.
story.tutorial.c1.plate.chip: Smelt a titanium plate at the forge
story.tutorial.c1.plate.hint: The forge works off the ship only: stay within a few steps of it while you craft. Inside your ship, smelting needs the Refinery module.
story.tutorial.c1.next.start: Titanium plates open bigger blueprints: the Titanium Drill for titanium ore, the terrain scanner, even a ship of your own. Each blueprint lists what it needs.
story.tutorial.c2.kinds.start: Plants, animals and rocks each teach you something. Scan 3 things you have never scanned before — every new find adds knowledge.
story.tutorial.c2.kinds.chip: Scan 3 new plants, animals or rocks
story.tutorial.c2.kinds.hint: Pick the scanner and press {key:Scan} on anything you haven't scanned yet — a strange plant, a new rock, an animal.
story.tutorial.c2.cache.start: Bigger blueprints need data fragments. Data caches are glowing blocks deep in the rock — mine one and it gives you two.
story.tutorial.c2.cache.hint: Data caches hide in caves and deep underground. Dig down a few blocks or follow a cave, with your lamp on.
story.tutorial.c2.costs.start: Every blueprint shows what it costs: knowledge, materials and sometimes data fragments. At your cockpit: menu ({key:UiMenu}), Blueprints.
story.tutorial.c2.costs.hint: Not enough knowledge? Scan new things. Short of materials? Each blueprint lists exactly what it needs.
story.tutorial.c2.cube.start: Glowing data cubes hold little games. Press {key:Interact} at one to download it, then play it under DataQubes in your menu — it teaches knowledge.
story.tutorial.c2.cube.hint: Your games are in the menu ({key:UiMenu}), behind the DataQubes button at the top. Every new star you earn is knowledge.
story.tutorial.c2.runes.start: Rune stones tell old stories. One stands on this world that you haven't read yet: walk up to it and scan its runes ({key:Scan}).
story.tutorial.c2.runes.hint: Look for tall, carved stones on the surface. Walk close and scan one.
story.tutorial.c2.scanner.start: The terrain scanner makes ore and data caches glow through rock. Craft it at your workshop, hold it and press {key:Place}.
story.tutorial.c2.scanner.hint: Its recipe needs titanium plates, cables, data fragments and an energy cell: menu ({key:UiMenu}), Crafting.
story.tutorial.c2.scanner.start_later: Later, the terrain scanner makes ore and data caches glow through rock. Its blueprint needs titanium plates — a forge makes them.
story.tutorial.c2.scanner.start_research: Now you can make titanium plates: research the terrain scanner under Blueprints, craft it, then hold it and press {key:Place} to see ore through rock.
story.tutorial.c2.progress.start: Your Achievements tab shows what you have done and what could come next. Open it in the menu ({key:UiMenu}).
story.tutorial.c3.waypoint.start: In flight, open the chart with {key:FlightMap} and click a world: it becomes your waypoint. An AI core Mk2 flies you there with {key:FlightAutopilot}.
story.tutorial.c3.waypoint.chip: Set a waypoint on the chart
story.tutorial.c3.waypoint.hint: Launch first — the chart works in flight. Click any world or station on it; an arrow then points the way.
story.tutorial.c3.planet.start: Scan a world before you land: pick the ship scanner, aim at a planet and hold fire until the ring is full. Its card shows air, dangers and riches.
story.tutorial.c3.planet.hint: The ship scanner sits on the last slot of your flight bar. Aboard your landed ship, the Map tab has a Planet scan button too.
story.tutorial.c3.asteroid.start: Your ship's laser breaks asteroids: aim and keep firing. Big rocks split into smaller ones, and the tractor beam pulls the chunks into your hold.
story.tutorial.c3.asteroid.hint: Asteroids drift near worlds and in belts. Pick the laser in your flight bar, fly close and keep firing.
story.tutorial.c3.inside.start: In flight, {key:FlightEnterInterior} lets you get up and walk around inside your ship. Try it — the cockpit takes you back to the helm.
story.tutorial.c3.eva.start: Walk out through the hatch while your ship floats in space: a spacewalk! Your suit uses its own air out there, so don't stay too long.
story.tutorial.c3.eva.hint: Step inside your floating ship, then walk out through the door. To get back aboard, float to the ship and press {key:Interact}.
story.tutorial.c3.target.start: When enemies show up, {key:FlightTargetNext} locks onto the next target — an arrow then shows you where it is.
story.tutorial.c3.zero_g.start: You're floating above the air! Let go and you sink back slowly — {key:Crouch} sinks faster, {key:Jump} rises. Up here your suit uses its own air.
story.tutorial.c4.dock.start: Let's visit a space station. Fly to one and press {key:Interact} near it — your ship parks itself.
story.tutorial.c4.dock.hint: Stations show on your radar and on the chart ({key:FlightMap}). Fly close until you can dock.
story.tutorial.c4.dock.start_settlement: No station in reach here — no problem: settlements trade and hand out jobs just the same.
story.tutorial.c4.market.start: Every vendor has a trade — miners, traders, researchers, settlers — and sells their own goods. Researchers even sell data fragments. Make a swap.
story.tutorial.c4.market.hint: Talk to a vendor with {key:Interact} and choose Trade. Each one only offers the swaps of their own trade.
story.tutorial.c4.job.start: The mission board lists jobs. Survey jobs (scan something) pay knowledge, others pay items. Take one — your menu's Missions tab keeps track.
story.tutorial.c4.job.chip: Take a job from the board
story.tutorial.c4.job.hint: Walk up to the mission board and press {key:Interact}. Pick a job you can manage.
story.tutorial.c4.undock.start: Ready to go? {key:Disembark} undocks you — your ship waits right outside where you parked it.
story.tutorial.c4.turnin.start: Do your job, then hand it in at the board where you took it. The Missions tab in your menu shows what is still missing.
story.tutorial.c4.turnin.chip: Hand your job in at its board
story.tutorial.c4.turnin.hint: A job is handed in where you took it. Back at that board, press {key:Interact} and choose Turn in.
story.tutorial.c5.marker.start: On a world, the planet map ({key:PlanetMap}) shows what you have explored. Set a marker on it — or ping a spot with {key:PingMarker}.
story.tutorial.c5.marker.chip: Set a marker or ping a spot
story.tutorial.c5.marker.hint: Markers stay on your map and compass. A ping is quick: aim at a spot and press {key:PingMarker} — friends see it too.
story.tutorial.c5.travel.start: A star system is a sun with its worlds. Worlds you have visited are on the map: travel to one — a parked ship flies the whole trip by itself.
story.tutorial.c5.travel.start_instant: A star system is a sun with its worlds. The map takes you to any of them in one go: travel to another world.
story.tutorial.c5.travel.chip: Travel to a world via the map
story.tutorial.c5.forge.start: Jump drives run on lubricant, and lubricant comes from a forge. Craft one at your workshop: 6 stone and 4 iron plates, no blueprint needed.
story.tutorial.c5.lube.start: Place your forge on a world. There, crude oil or 3 biofuel plus carbon become lubricant. Make some — the jump generator needs it.
story.tutorial.c5.lube.hint: Crude oil sits in dark pockets underground; a fluid pump pulls it up. Biofuel is the way without oil.
story.tutorial.c5.radar.start: The jump generator needs the Radar Array blueprint first: 45 knowledge, plus data fragments and titanium plates. Research it under Blueprints.
story.tutorial.c5.radar.hint: Knowledge comes from new scans, data fragments from data caches and researchers, titanium plates from a forge.
story.tutorial.c5.jumpbp.start: Now the Jump Generator itself: 90 knowledge, data fragments, titanium plates and energy cells. Research it under Blueprints.
story.tutorial.c5.module.start: Build the Jump Generator module at your ship's workshop: menu ({key:UiMenu}), Ship. It's a big build — the list shows what's still missing.
story.tutorial.c5.module.chip: Fit the Jump Generator to your ship
story.tutorial.c5.module.hint: Modules are built aboard, next to the workshop, in the Ship tab. Each kind fits once.
story.tutorial.c5.jump.start: Your jump drive is ready! Open the chart ({key:FlightMap}), go to the Hyperspace tab, pick a star and jump.
story.tutorial.c5.jump.hint: Any star on the Hyperspace tab is fine for a first jump. You can always jump back the same way.
story.tutorial.c5.wormhole.start: Wormholes are shortcuts between far systems — no jump drive needed. Fly up to one, press {key:Interact} and fly through.
story.tutorial.c5.salvage.start: Wrecks and debris fields drift in many systems, full of salvage. Fly to one, or collect a capsule from a debris field.
story.tutorial.c5.salvage.chip: Find a wreck or a salvage capsule
story.tutorial.c5.salvage.hint: Their signals show on the chart ({key:FlightMap}). Click one and fly there — with an AI core Mk2, {key:FlightAutopilot} flies for you.
story.tutorial.c6.module.start: Modules give your ship cargo space, shields, weapons and more. Aboard, open menu ({key:UiMenu}), Ship, and build one — each kind fits once.
story.tutorial.c6.module.hint: Most modules need their blueprint first. The Ship tab lists what each one still needs — and taking one out gives half of it back.
story.tutorial.c6.repair.start: Your hull is damaged — it never heals by itself. Press {key:RepairWreck} at your ship's console: each iron plate buys 10 hull points.
story.tutorial.c6.repair.hint: Carry iron plates in your backpack or the hold. Holes in the hull are refilled too, as far as your materials go.
story.tutorial.c6.repair.start_later: If your hull ever takes damage: press {key:RepairWreck} at your ship's console with iron plates in your pack. A hull never heals by itself.
story.tutorial.c6.grow.start: Your ship can grow: while it is parked, build onto it or furnish the cabin with {key:Place}. Up to 15 blocks each way — sealed rooms keep their air.
story.tutorial.c6.grow.hint: Aim at your parked ship and place a block so it touches the hull. The cabin takes furniture and lamps too.
story.tutorial.c6.titanium.start: A ship of your own needs the Shipwright blueprint, and that needs titanium plates. Take the short course “Workshop and titanium” in your Journal first.
story.tutorial.c6.blueprint.start: Your own ship starts with the Shipwright blueprint: 40 knowledge, 3 data fragments, 8 titanium plates, 2 circuit boards. Research it under Blueprints.
story.tutorial.c6.blueprint.hint: Knowledge comes from new scans, data fragments from data caches, titanium plates from your forge, circuit boards from gold, silver and silicate.
story.tutorial.c6.keel.start: Craft a Ship Keel at your workshop and place it on solid ground — your new ship will be built right there, around it.
story.tutorial.c6.keel.hint: The keel takes metal panels, circuit boards and energy cells. Only one ship can be under construction at a time.
story.tutorial.c6.commission.start: Build around the keel: a hull, one Ship Helm, a Ship Engine and a door, sealed all round. Then press {key:Interact} at the helm to commission it.
story.tutorial.c6.commission.hint: At the helm, {key:Interact} tells you what is still missing — a helm, an engine, a door or a gap in the hull. Up to 15 blocks each way.
story.tutorial.c6.switch.start: Your ships form a fleet. In the menu's Ship tab, pick one under “Your ships” and choose “Switch to” — try your old ship again.
story.tutorial.c7.core.start: A Base Core makes this world your home. Craft one at your ship's workshop — 6 stone and 2 iron plates, no blueprint — and place it where you want to live.
story.tutorial.c7.core.hint: One base per world. Later, press {key:Interact} at the stone to give your base a name. An ally's base counts too.
story.tutorial.c7.zone.start: This is your base zone: the cube around the core. Here you build freely, the air stays good and animals keep their distance. Place 10 blocks in it.
story.tutorial.c7.zone.chip: Place 10 blocks in your base zone
story.tutorial.c7.zone.hint: The zone reaches 8 blocks from the core in every direction. Allies may build in it too; nobody else can.
story.tutorial.c7.light.start: Light it up: place 2 lights in your base — torches (crafted by hand from wood and plant fibre), lanterns, lamps or a campfire.
story.tutorial.c7.light.hint: Torches are the quickest: 1 wood and 2 plant fibre make 4, by hand. Place them inside your base zone.
story.tutorial.c7.door.start: Doors: craft a Wooden Door by hand from 4 wood, hang it in a gap in your wall and open it with {key:Interact}.
story.tutorial.c7.door.chip: Hang a door and open it
story.tutorial.c7.door.hint: Place the door like a block, right in the gap. Nothing can be built where a door hangs.
story.tutorial.c7.air.start: On an airless world a sealed room holds air: walls and a roof of stone, metal or glass around your core. Only an Energy Door keeps the air in.
story.tutorial.c7.air.chip: Seal a room at your base
story.tutorial.c7.air.hint: Aim at the core: it tells you whether a room holds air. Dirt, sand, gaps and other doors leak.
story.tutorial.c7.air.start_later: On airless worlds your core gives air too — in the cube around it and in every sealed room of stone, metal or glass, shut by an Energy Door.
story.tutorial.c7.walls.start: No wild animal appears close to your core. A closed ring of walls, 2 blocks high, keeps them out further: build one around your base and step inside.
story.tutorial.c7.walls.chip: Close a wall ring and stand inside
story.tutorial.c7.walls.hint: Stand under the open sky inside the ring — a room or a cave does not count. The ring may be up to 48 blocks from the core; one gap or an open wooden door lets animals in.
story.tutorial.c7.bed.start: A bed makes your base the place you wake up. Craft one by hand (6 wood, 8 plant fibre), place it and press {key:Interact} at it.
story.tutorial.c7.bed.chip: Make a bed your wake-up spot
story.tutorial.c7.bed.hint: Stand right next to the bed when you press {key:Interact}. A heal tank works as a wake-up spot too.
story.tutorial.c7.residents.start: Settlers may move into your base and work at posts you build. Visitors drop by now and then — not every one is friendly, so keep your walls closed.
story.tutorial.c17.core.start: A station of your own starts with a Station Core: craft one at your workshop, go on a spacewalk and deploy it with {key:EvaDeployStation}.
story.tutorial.c17.core.hint: The core takes 6 metal panels, 2 circuit boards and an Energy Cell I. For a spacewalk, step out through your floating ship's hatch.
story.tutorial.c17.hull.start: Build around the core on your spacewalk ({key:Place}): a small hull of a dozen blocks and a door as its airlock. Then your station is commissioned.
story.tutorial.c17.hull.hint: Every new block must touch one that is already there. Any door counts as the airlock; an Energy Door also keeps the air in.
story.tutorial.c17.zero_g.start: Board your station with {key:Interact} next to it. Aboard, {key:ToggleStationZeroG} lets you float while you build — press it again to walk.
story.tutorial.c17.zero_g.hint: Zero-g building works on your own stations. Floating, you can reach the outer walls from inside.
story.tutorial.c8.net.start: The comm radio opened the Crystal Net: crystal wires that carry one signal, ON or OFF. Research its first blueprint, “Crystal Net”, under Blueprints.
story.tutorial.c8.net.hint: It costs knowledge, 2 data fragments, 4 crystals and a circuit board. Glowing plants and crystal rock drop crystals.
story.tutorial.c8.handin.hint: Does it work? Hand the job in: menu ({key:UiMenu}), Missions — the reward is yours. The Codex's Crystal Net pages show every part.
story.tutorial.c8.light.start: My first workshop job, “First Light”, waits in your Missions tab. Lay a switch, a line of conduits and a lamp, touching — flip the switch with {key:Interact}: the line glows!
story.tutorial.c8.light.chip: Job 1: a switch lights a lamp
story.tutorial.c8.bell.start: Job 2, “Doorbell”, waits in your Missions tab: a step plate outside, a chime inside, conduits between them. Step on the plate — ding dong!
story.tutorial.c8.bell.start_research: Job 2 is a doorbell. It needs the blueprint “Crystal Sound” first: research it under Blueprints, then take the job in your Missions tab.
story.tutorial.c8.bell.chip: Job 2: a step plate rings a chime
story.tutorial.c8.night.start: Job 3, “Night Light”: a daylight sensor set to “ON at night”, conduits and a lamp. When the sun goes down, the lamp switches itself on.
story.tutorial.c8.night.start_research: Job 3 is a night light. It needs the blueprint “Crystal Senses” first — sensors that notice day, night and visitors. Research it under Blueprints.
story.tutorial.c8.night.chip: Job 3: nightfall switches a lamp on
story.tutorial.c8.airlock.start: Job 4, “Airlock”: a logic block set to NOT, its arrow at a conduit beside a door. A wired door shows a lamp: red locked, green open. NOT with no input is ON — green!
story.tutorial.c8.airlock.start_research: Job 4 is an airlock. It needs the blueprint “Crystal Logic” first — blocks that decide: AND, OR, NOT. Research it under Blueprints.
story.tutorial.c8.airlock.chip: Job 4: a logic block opens a door
story.tutorial.c8.machine.start: Job 5, “Little Factory”: start a fabricator, a drill or a matter sender with a button or a timer block. The machine must really finish its job.
story.tutorial.c8.machine.start_research: Job 5 is a little factory. It needs the blueprint “Fabricator” first: a machine that crafts from the crates beside it. Research it under Blueprints.
story.tutorial.c8.machine.chip: Job 5: a signal starts a machine
story.tutorial.c8.secret.start: Job 6, “Secret Passage”: a wall of phase blocks wired to a switch or a step plate. Signal ON and the whole wall opens — dye it like your walls and nobody finds it.
story.tutorial.c8.secret.start_research: Job 6 is a secret door. It needs “Crystal Mechanics” first — blocks that move: phase blocks, trapdoors, bridge motors. Research it under Blueprints.
story.tutorial.c8.secret.chip: Job 6: a signal opens a phase wall
story.tutorial.c14.terminal.start: A factory's terminal crafts in bulk: cheap raw ore in, plates and parts out — anyone may use it. Stand at the terminal and craft something: menu ({key:UiMenu}), Crafting.
story.tutorial.c14.terminal.chip: Craft something at a factory terminal
story.tutorial.c14.terminal.hint: Each factory makes only a few things — the terminal lists them. The raw ore comes from your backpack.
story.tutorial.c14.terminal.start_later: Factories are rare halls with working machines. When you find one, craft at its terminal: cheap raw ore in, plates and parts out, in bulk.
story.tutorial.c14.claim.start: An SPS code — from a treasure chest or a trader — claims a factory: press {key:Interact} at its terminal. It becomes your base; you and your allies may rebuild it.
story.tutorial.c14.claimed.start: This factory is yours now: you and your allies may rebuild it, and its terminal still crafts for everyone.
story.tutorial.c14.wait.start: A fabricator that works by itself needs a machine circuit (my fifth workshop job) and a forge's goods (the course “Workshop and titanium”). This course waits for both.
story.tutorial.c14.line.start: Now an assembly line: a fabricator, its recipe set with {key:Interact}, crates with the inputs beside it. Wire a switch to it and leave it ON — it crafts by itself.
story.tutorial.c14.line.chip: Let a fabricator craft twice by itself
story.tutorial.c14.line.hint: An amber light means something is missing: the inputs in a crate beside it, room for the result, or a forge beside it for smelting. Stay near — it crafts for you.
story.tutorial.c14.away.start: Leave machines running when you go: when you come back, they catch up on the work they missed (up to this world's limit), and I sum it up for you.
story.tutorial.c14.away.start_off: On this world machines rest while nobody is around — they carry on when you are back. Timers and sounds simply start again.
story.tutorial.c9.scan.start: Most animals are calm. Scan one with {key:Scan}: the readout says how it behaves and what it loves — “Aggressive” means keep your distance.
story.tutorial.c9.scan.start_calm: The animals on this world are all peaceful. Scan one with {key:Scan}: the readout says how it lives and which food it loves most.
story.tutorial.c9.scan.hint: Animals graze in the open, swim in the water or hide in caves. Point at one and hold {key:Scan} until the readout opens.
story.tutorial.c9.feed.start: Some herds beg for food. Hold something to eat and wait — when they come hopping over, {key:FeedCreature} throws them a piece.
story.tutorial.c9.feed.hint: Berries and fruit work for many animals. Stand still with the food in your hand — not every kind of animal begs.
story.tutorial.c9.tame.start: To tame an animal, throw it its favourite food a few times — or calm it with a creature translator. Then it stays with you as a companion.
story.tutorial.c9.tame.hint: A scan shows what an animal loves (“Loves: …”). The translator, a blueprint, reads the mood of animals that do not beg.
story.tutorial.c9.care.start: Your companion follows you on its home world. Give it a name in the Creatures tab, or feed it — a strong bond makes it fetch things for you.
story.tutorial.c9.care.hint: Menu {key:UiMenu}, tab Creatures. To feed it, carry food it likes and stand close to it.
story.tutorial.c10.plant.start: Plants grow while you play. Make seeds or saplings by hand — from fibre, berries or wood — and plant one on soil with {key:Place}.
story.tutorial.c10.plant.chip: Plant a seed or a sapling
story.tutorial.c10.plant.hint: Seeds and saplings are hand recipes in the crafting menu. Grass and dirt take them; inside your base a flower pot or a hydro tray works too.
story.tutorial.c10.cook.start: A campfire is a little kitchen: stand at it and cook there — a hot meal fills you up better. It turns wood into torches, too.
story.tutorial.c10.cook.start_nohunger: A campfire is a little workshop: stand at it and craft there — torches from wood, water from ice, salt from water.
story.tutorial.c10.cook.hint: Place a campfire, stand next to it and open the crafting menu — its recipes show up there.
story.tutorial.c10.sample.start: Your suit carries a sample case: harvest a plant, a tree or some ore, and a sample of it goes in by itself.
story.tutorial.c10.sample.hint: Mine a flower or a bush — or some ore. Animals give samples too: the sampler takes one without hurting them.
story.tutorial.c10.research.start: A bio lab tells you what is in a sample. Research its blueprint at your cockpit — it needs knowledge, data fragments, glass and fibre.
story.tutorial.c10.research.hint: The Blueprints tab shows what the Bio Lab still needs. Data fragments hide in data caches deep in the rock.
story.tutorial.c10.lab.start: Build the bio lab at the workshop and set it up on the ground — or fit the lab module to your ship. Then analyse a sample there.
story.tutorial.c10.lab.chip: Analyse a sample in the bio lab
story.tutorial.c10.lab.hint: Stand at the lab and press {key:Interact}. Pick a sample on the Analyse page — each kind needs it only once.
story.tutorial.c10.lab.done: Now you know what it does. Mix it next: one sample alone gives an extract you can take — later you can even change your gear with it.
story.tutorial.c11.talk.start: People live in settlements. Walk up to someone and press {key:Interact} to talk — traders, farmers, guards, a doctor.
story.tutorial.c11.talk.hint: Your map {key:PlanetMap} shows settlements nearby. People walk between the houses — at night most of them sleep.
story.tutorial.c11.answer.start: Answers matter: kind replies turn a stranger into an acquaintance, then a friend. Pick an answer when someone has something to say.
story.tutorial.c11.answer.hint: Not everyone has something to talk about right now — try another person, or come back later.
story.tutorial.c11.people.start: Friends tell you where things are and call you on the radio. The Settings tab lists the people you know — have a look.
story.tutorial.c11.people.hint: Menu {key:UiMenu}, tab Settings: the list “People you know” shows everyone and how well you know them.
story.tutorial.c11.jobs.start: Settlers help in their own way: the doctor heals you, the sage sells knowledge, traders swap goods — and the board has jobs.
story.tutorial.c12.robbers.start: Robbers may stop you and ask for your things. Pay, and they leave — or say no and chase them away. Their camps can be cleared for a reward.
story.tutorial.c12.fend.start: It is always your choice: walk away — or fend off what attacks you with {key:PrimaryFire}. A tool or a weapon works much better than bare hands.
story.tutorial.c12.fend.hint: Armour softens hits, and a stasis projector freezes an attacker. If your health runs low, back off — if you faint, you wake up again.
story.tutorial.c12.space.start: In space, hostile ships shoot from far away and your laser reaches a little less: fly in close, keep your shields up and chase one away.
story.tutorial.c12.space.hint: {key:FlightTargetNext} picks a target. A shield module from the workshop helps a lot — repair the hull afterwards.
story.tutorial.c13.climb.start: You can climb almost any wall: jump at it, push towards it and hold {key:Jump}. Let go to slide down. Climbing gloves let you hold on longer.
story.tutorial.c13.climb.hint: Any steep rock, tree trunk or house wall works — not glass. Sand and snow crumble, and ice needs climbing claws.
story.tutorial.c13.rope.start: The energy rope gun shoots a rope that sticks to any block up to 24 blocks away. Hold it, aim at a wall or a ledge and fire.
story.tutorial.c13.rope.hint: Craft the rope gun at the workshop and put it in your quick bar. Each shot costs a little suit energy.
story.tutorial.c13.rope.done: It holds! Hold {key:Place} to reel yourself in, let go to hang, and {key:Crouch} drops the rope. Aim at a cliff top to be pulled over the edge.
story.tutorial.c13.rope.start_later: Later: the energy rope gun (a blueprint after the climbing gloves) shoots a rope that holds you — up a cliff or across a gap.
story.tutorial.c13.fly.start: Wear the jetpack or the glider on your back. The jetpack lifts you while you hold {key:Jump}; the glider opens while you fall — hold {key:Jump}.
story.tutorial.c13.fly.chip: Fly with the jetpack or glider
story.tutorial.c13.fly.hint: Both are made at the workshop and worn in the back slot. The glider needs air — on airless worlds it stays folded.
story.tutorial.c13.ride.start: A boat needs no blueprint: craft it at the workshop, use it at the shore and board it with {key:Interact}. A speeder drives over land the same way.
story.tutorial.c13.ride.chip: Ride a boat or a speeder
story.tutorial.c13.ride.hint: Hold the boat, face the water and use it — it lands in front of you. {key:StowVehicle} packs a vehicle away again.
story.tutorial.c13.train.start: A monorail runs on this world. Walk to a stop, step into the cab with {key:Interact} and ride along.
story.tutorial.c13.train.chip: Take a ride on a train
story.tutorial.c13.train.hint: Trains stop at their stops by themselves — wait there, or follow the pylons until you see one.
story.tutorial.c13.train.start_later: Later you can build your own monorail: pylons, a line and a cab. Some worlds already have trains between their towns.
story.tutorial.c13.beam.start: Beam blocks link your places on a world: stand on one, press {key:Interact} and pick another. Lifts carry you up and down in your base.
story.tutorial.c15.chat.start: Press {key:OpenChat}, type a line and send it. Your radio decides who hears you: this world, the star system, or the whole galaxy.
story.tutorial.c15.chat.start_radio: Chat needs a radio you wear: research the Comm Radio, craft it and put it on. Then {key:OpenChat} opens the chat.
story.tutorial.c15.chat.chip_radio: Wear a radio and send a chat line
story.tutorial.c15.chat.hint: Wear the radio in a module slot of your suit. A system or galaxy radio reaches further.
story.tutorial.c15.trade.start: Trade face to face: stand close to another player and press {key:RequestTrade}. Both put things in, both confirm — done.
story.tutorial.c15.trade.hint: Ask in the chat first — a trade only starts when the other player agrees.
story.tutorial.c15.ally.start: Allies share their bases and stations and never hurt each other. Ask someone in the Alliances tab — or start a crew and invite your friends.
story.tutorial.c15.ally.chip: Become allies or join a crew
story.tutorial.c15.ally.hint: Both of you have to agree. Either of you can end an alliance at any time.
story.tutorial.c15.ping.start: Show your allies a spot: look at it and press {key:PingMarker}. Your allies and your crew on this world see the pin for half a minute.
story.tutorial.c15.ping.hint: Look at the spot first — the pin lands where you aim.
story.tutorial.c15.kind.start: Be kind — everyone here is a real person. If someone is unkind, mute them, and type /report: a person will look at it.
story.tutorial.c16.paint.start: The paint tool draws on blocks. Research it and craft it at the workshop, then point it at a placed block, press {key:Place} and paint a picture.
story.tutorial.c16.paint.hint: It is a cheap blueprint: berries and an iron plate. Mining a painted block loses the paint — save the pictures you like.
story.tutorial.c16.form.start: Blocks can take other forms: slopes, stairs, slabs. Pick a stack in your quick bar, press {key:HotbarAction} and choose Form. The shaping tool even designs your own.
story.tutorial.c16.form.chip: Give a block a new form
story.tutorial.c16.form.hint: Only building materials take forms — stone, wood, metal, glass. Your own forms wait under “My forms” in the Forms tab of the crafting menu.
story.tutorial.c16.colour.start: The same slot actions colour blocks: choose Colour and pick one. Dye is free; glowing blocks cost a crystal each.
story.tutorial.c16.colour.hint: Dye recolours the whole stack at once. Lamps and torches take dye too and then shine in that colour.
story.tutorial.c16.copy.start: The blueprint tool copies a whole build: use it on two corner blocks to copy it, then paste the copy somewhere else, block by block from your backpack.
story.tutorial.c16.copy.hint: Craft it at the workshop — no blueprint needed. A copy is at most 16 blocks each way, and the paste needs the blocks in your backpack.
story.tutorial.c16.look.start: Make it yours: change your colours and draw your face in the Settings tab. A camera takes photos for the Photos tab.
story.tutorial.c18.loot.start: Old chests and caches hide in ruins, caves and wrecks. Stand at one and press {key:LootContainer} to take what is inside.
story.tutorial.c18.loot.chip: Empty a chest or a cache
story.tutorial.c18.loot.hint: Your backpack needs room for it all — what does not fit stays inside. Settlers sometimes tell you where one is.
story.tutorial.c18.ruin.start: Buried ruins and crashed wrecks hold old tech. When I sense one close by, I tell you — walk up to it and bring the scanner.
story.tutorial.c18.ruin.chip: Reach a ruin or a wreck
story.tutorial.c18.ruin.hint: Look around as you travel — I speak up when something is in reach. Your map {key:PlanetMap} keeps what you have found.
story.tutorial.c18.ruin.start_none: This world has no buried ruins or crashed wrecks. Keep your eyes open anyway: chests hide in caves and old towns.
story.tutorial.c18.tips.start: Settlers who like you point out hidden chests on your map. Glowing data cubes hold games: press {key:Interact} at one to download it.
story.tutorial.c18.wreck.start: Wrecks drift in space too. When I pick up a wreck's signal, fly there — salvage waits inside, and old logs tell their story.
story.tutorial.c18.wreck.hint: Set the wreck as your waypoint on the chart {key:FlightMap}. A debris field counts too.
